lab_questions.title: Practical SQL Evaluation
lab_questions.description: Evaluate candidates on their practical SQL skills across various domains.

tasks.title: E-Commerce: Top 3 Customers by Total Spend
tasks.description: Given two tables, `customers` (id, name, email) and `orders` (id, customer_id, amount, order_date), write a SQL query to retrieve the names and emails of the top 3 customers who have spent the most in total. The result should include `name`, `email`, and `total_spent`.

scoring_rules.system_query: SELECT c.name, c.email, SUM(o.amount) as total_spent FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.id, c.name, c.email ORDER BY total_spent DESC LIMIT 3;

solution.query.sql: SELECT c.name, c.email, SUM(o.amount) as total_spent FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.id, c.name, c.email ORDER BY total_spent DESC LIMIT 3;

tasks.title: HR: Second Highest Salary per Department
tasks.description: Given two tables, `employees` (id, name, salary, department_id) and `departments` (id, name), write a SQL query to find the employee with the second highest salary in each department. Use Window Functions. Output should be `department_name`, `employee_name`, and `salary`.

scoring_rules.system_query: WITH RankedSalaries AS (SELECT d.name as department_name, e.name as employee_name, e.salary, DENSE_RANK() OVER(PARTITION BY e.department_id ORDER BY e.salary DESC) as rn FROM employees e JOIN departments d ON e.department_id = d.id) SELECT department_name, employee_name, salary FROM RankedSalaries WHERE rn = 2;

solution.query.sql: WITH RankedSalaries AS (SELECT d.name as department_name, e.name as employee_name, e.salary, DENSE_RANK() OVER(PARTITION BY e.department_id ORDER BY e.salary DESC) as rn FROM employees e JOIN departments d ON e.department_id = d.id) SELECT department_name, employee_name, salary FROM RankedSalaries WHERE rn = 2;

tasks.title: Finance: 7-Day Rolling Average of Transactions
tasks.description: Given a table `transactions` (transaction_id, amount, transaction_date), write a SQL query to calculate the 7-day rolling average of total transaction amounts for each day. The result should include `transaction_date` and `rolling_avg`.

scoring_rules.system_query: WITH daily_totals AS (SELECT transaction_date, SUM(amount) AS daily_total FROM transactions GROUP BY transaction_date) SELECT transaction_date, AVG(daily_total) OVER (ORDER BY transaction_date ROWS BETWEEN 6 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS rolling_avg FROM daily_totals ORDER BY transaction_date;

solution.query.sql: WITH daily_totals AS (SELECT transaction_date, SUM(amount) AS daily_total FROM transactions GROUP BY transaction_date) SELECT transaction_date, AVG(daily_total) OVER (ORDER BY transaction_date ROWS BETWEEN 6 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS rolling_avg FROM daily_totals ORDER BY transaction_date;

tasks.title: Sales: Products with No Sales in 6 Months
tasks.description: Given two tables, `products` (id, name, category) and `sales` (id, product_id, sale_date, quantity), write a SQL query to identify all products that have not been sold in the last 6 months from the current date. Include `product_id` and `product_name`.

scoring_rules.system_query: SELECT u.username FROM users u JOIN likes l ON u.id = l.user_id JOIN posts p ON l.post_id = p.id WHERE p.author_id = (SELECT id FROM users WHERE username = 'influencer_x') GROUP BY u.id, u.username HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT p.id) = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM posts WHERE author_id = (SELECT id FROM users WHERE username = 'influencer_x'));

solution.query.sql: SELECT p.id as product_id, p.name as product_name FROM products p LEFT JOIN sales s ON p.id = s.product_id AND s.sale_date >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '6 months' WHERE s.id IS NULL;

tasks.title: Social Media: Users Who Liked All Posts by a Specific User
tasks.description: Given tables `users` (id, username), `posts` (id, author_id, content), and `likes` (user_id, post_id), write a query to find the usernames of all users who have liked EVERY single post created by the user with username 'influencer_x'.

scoring_rules.system_query: SELECT p.name, COUNT(v.id) as visit_count FROM patients p JOIN visits v ON p.id = v.patient_id WHERE v.visit_date >= '2023-11-01' AND v.visit_date <= '2023-11-30' GROUP BY p.id, p.name HAVING COUNT(v.id) > 1;

solution.query.sql: SELECT u.username FROM users u JOIN likes l ON u.id = l.user_id JOIN posts p ON l.post_id = p.id WHERE p.author_id = (SELECT id FROM users WHERE username = 'influencer_x') GROUP BY u.id, u.username HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT p.id) = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM posts WHERE author_id = (SELECT id FROM users WHERE username = 'influencer_x'));

tasks.title: Healthcare: Patients with Multiple Visits in a Month
tasks.description: Given two tables, `patients` (id, name) and `visits` (id, patient_id, visit_date), write a SQL query to find the names of patients who have visited more than once in November 2023. Include `name` and `visit_count`.

scoring_rules.system_query: SELECT s.name, AVG(g.grade) as avg_grade FROM students s JOIN grades g ON s.id = g.student_id GROUP BY s.id, s.name HAVING AVG(g.grade) > 80;

solution.query.sql: SELECT p.name, COUNT(v.id) as visit_count FROM patients p JOIN visits v ON p.id = v.patient_id WHERE v.visit_date >= '2023-11-01' AND v.visit_date <= '2023-11-30' GROUP BY p.id, p.name HAVING COUNT(v.id) > 1;

tasks.title: Education: Students with Average Grade Above 80
tasks.description: Given two tables, `students` (id, name) and `grades` (id, student_id, course, grade), write a SQL query to retrieve the names of students whose average grade across all courses is strictly greater than 80. Include `name` and `avg_grade`.

scoring_rules.system_query: SELECT p.id as product_id, p.name as product_name FROM products p LEFT JOIN sales s ON p.id = s.product_id AND s.sale_date >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '6 months' WHERE s.id IS NULL;

solution.query.sql: SELECT s.name, AVG(g.grade) as avg_grade FROM students s JOIN grades g ON s.id = g.student_id GROUP BY s.id, s.name HAVING AVG(g.grade) > 80;

lab_questions.title: Practical PostgreSQL Evaluation
lab_questions.description: Evaluate candidates on practical PostgreSQL skills for FinTech and SaaS analytics including aggregations, HAVING filters, Window Functions, and multi-table reconciliation.

tasks.title: Task 1: Active Monthly Recurring Revenue (MRR) by Plan
tasks.description: Given table `subscriptions` (id, user_id, plan_name, monthly_amount, status, start_date), write a PostgreSQL query to calculate total Monthly Recurring Revenue (`total_mrr`) and active subscriber count (`active_subscribers`) for each plan where status is 'ACTIVE'. Order by `total_mrr` DESC.

scoring_rules.system_query: SELECT plan_name, COUNT(id) AS active_subscribers, SUM(monthly_amount) AS total_mrr FROM subscriptions WHERE status = 'ACTIVE' GROUP BY plan_name ORDER BY total_mrr DESC;

solution.query.sql: SELECT plan_name, COUNT(id) AS active_subscribers, SUM(monthly_amount) AS total_mrr FROM subscriptions WHERE status = 'ACTIVE' GROUP BY plan_name ORDER BY total_mrr DESC;

tasks.title: Task 2: High-Volume Accounts with Failed Audit Events
tasks.description: Given tables `accounts` (id, account_number, balance, tier) and `audit_logs` (id, account_id, action, performed_at, status_code), write a PostgreSQL query to identify all account numbers that have experienced more than 2 failed actions (status_code >= 400). Return `account_number` and `failed_count`, ordered by `failed_count` DESC.

scoring_rules.system_query: SELECT a.account_number, COUNT(l.id) AS failed_count FROM accounts a JOIN audit_logs l ON a.id = l.account_id WHERE l.status_code >= 400 GROUP BY a.id, a.account_number HAVING COUNT(l.id) > 2 ORDER BY failed_count DESC;

solution.query.sql: SELECT a.account_number, COUNT(l.id) AS failed_count FROM accounts a JOIN audit_logs l ON a.id = l.account_id WHERE l.status_code >= 400 GROUP BY a.id, a.account_number HAVING COUNT(l.id) > 2 ORDER BY failed_count DESC;

tasks.title: Task 3: Cumulative Running Revenue per Subscription
tasks.description: Given table `payments` (id, subscription_id, amount, payment_status, payment_date), write a PostgreSQL query using Window Functions (`SUM() OVER`) to calculate the cumulative running total revenue earned per subscription for all successful payments (`payment_status = 'SUCCESS'`). Include `subscription_id`, `payment_date`, `amount`, and `running_total`.

scoring_rules.system_query: SELECT subscription_id, payment_date, amount, SUM(amount) OVER(PARTITION BY subscription_id ORDER BY payment_date) AS running_total FROM payments WHERE payment_status = 'SUCCESS' ORDER BY subscription_id, payment_date;

solution.query.sql: SELECT subscription_id, payment_date, amount, SUM(amount) OVER(PARTITION BY subscription_id ORDER BY payment_date) AS running_total FROM payments WHERE payment_status = 'SUCCESS' ORDER BY subscription_id, payment_date;

tasks.title: Task 4: Subscriptions with No Successful Payments
tasks.description: Given tables `subscriptions` (id, user_id, plan_name, monthly_amount, status) and `payments` (id, subscription_id, amount, payment_status), write a PostgreSQL query to identify all subscriptions that have never had a single successful payment (`payment_status = 'SUCCESS'`). Return `subscription_id`, `plan_name`, and `status`, ordered by `subscription_id` ASC.

scoring_rules.system_query: SELECT s.id AS subscription_id, s.plan_name, s.status FROM subscriptions s LEFT JOIN payments p ON s.id = p.subscription_id AND p.payment_status = 'SUCCESS' WHERE p.id IS NULL ORDER BY s.id;

solution.query.sql: SELECT s.id AS subscription_id, s.plan_name, s.status FROM subscriptions s LEFT JOIN payments p ON s.id = p.subscription_id AND p.payment_status = 'SUCCESS' WHERE p.id IS NULL ORDER BY s.id;

lab_questions.title: Practical MongoDB Evaluation
lab_questions.description: Evaluate candidates on practical MongoDB NoSQL skills for SaaS and e-commerce analytics including CRUD operations, aggregation pipelines ($match, $group, $lookup, $unwind), complex projection, and indexing optimization.

tasks.title: Task 1: Top Performing Product Categories by Revenue
tasks.description: Given collection `orders` with documents having fields { id, customer_id, category, amount, status: 'paid' | 'pending' | 'refunded', order_date }, write a MongoDB aggregation query to calculate total revenue (`total_revenue`) and count of orders (`order_count`) for each category where status is 'paid'. Sort the results by `total_revenue` in descending order.

tasks.title: Task 2: High-Value Customer Activity with Multi-Document Lookup
tasks.description: Given collections `customers` ({ _id, name, tier, signup_date }) and `orders` ({ _id, customer_id, amount, status }), write an aggregation pipeline to join `customers` with their completed orders (`status: 'paid'`), filter for customers who have placed at least 3 paid orders, and return their `name`, `tier`, and `total_spent`, ordered by `total_spent` DESC.

scoring_rules.system_query: db.customers.aggregate([{ $lookup: { from: 'orders', localField: '_id', foreignField: 'customer_id', pipeline: [{ $match: { status: 'paid' } }], as: 'paid_orders' } }, { $addFields: { order_count: { $size: '$paid_orders' }, total_spent: { $sum: '$paid_orders.amount' } } }, { $match: { order_count: { $gte: 3 } } }, { $project: { _id: 0, name: 1, tier: 1, total_spent: 1, order_count: 1 } }, { $sort: { total_spent: -1 } }])

solution.query.js: db.customers.aggregate([{ $lookup: { from: 'orders', localField: '_id', foreignField: 'customer_id', pipeline: [{ $match: { status: 'paid' } }], as: 'paid_orders' } }, { $addFields: { order_count: { $size: '$paid_orders' }, total_spent: { $sum: '$paid_orders.amount' } } }, { $match: { order_count: { $gte: 3 } } }, { $project: { _id: 0, name: 1, tier: 1, total_spent: 1, order_count: 1 } }, { $sort: { total_spent: -1 } }]);

tasks.title: Task 3: Unwind Array Elements for Tag Frequency Analysis
tasks.description: Given collection `articles` ({ _id, title, author, tags: [String], views, published_year }), write a MongoDB aggregation query using `$unwind` to count the number of articles and calculate total views for each tag in articles published in 2024. Return `tag`, `article_count`, and `total_views`, sorted by `total_views` DESC.

scoring_rules.system_query: db.articles.aggregate([{ $match: { published_year: 2024 } }, { $unwind: '$tags' }, { $group: { _id: '$tags', article_count: { $sum: 1 }, total_views: { $sum: '$views' } } }, { $project: { tag: '$_id', _id: 0, article_count: 1, total_views: 1 } }, { $sort: { total_views: -1 } }])

solution.query.js: db.articles.aggregate([{ $match: { published_year: 2024 } }, { $unwind: '$tags' }, { $group: { _id: '$tags', article_count: { $sum: 1 }, total_views: { $sum: '$views' } } }, { $project: { tag: '$_id', _id: 0, article_count: 1, total_views: 1 } }, { $sort: { total_views: -1 } }]);

tasks.title: Task 4: Finding Inactive Users with Zero Orders in the Last 90 Days
tasks.description: Given collections `users` ({ _id, username, email, is_active: true }) and `user_activity_logs` ({ _id, user_id, action, timestamp }), write a MongoDB query to find all active users who have no logged activity in the last 90 days (`timestamp >= new Date('2024-06-01')`). Return `username` and `email` sorted by `username` ASC.

scoring_rules.system_query: db.users.aggregate([{ $match: { is_active: true } }, { $lookup: { from: 'user_activity_logs', localField: '_id', foreignField: 'user_id', pipeline: [{ $match: { timestamp: { $gte: new Date('2024-06-01') } } }], as: 'recent_logs' } }, { $match: { recent_logs: { $size: 0 } } }, { $project: { _id: 0, username: 1, email: 1 } }, { $sort: { username: 1 } }])

solution.query.js: db.users.aggregate([{ $match: { is_active: true } }, { $lookup: { from: 'user_activity_logs', localField: '_id', foreignField: 'user_id', pipeline: [{ $match: { timestamp: { $gte: new Date('2024-06-01') } } }], as: 'recent_logs' } }, { $match: { recent_logs: { $size: 0 } } }, { $project: { _id: 0, username: 1, email: 1 } }, { $sort: { username: 1 } }]);
